correctness.rationale: PASS: Klahn Theorems 2.1–2.2 (as checked in original preprint) reduce any all-prime monic solution to x^a times a cyclotomic product, and a nonpure power of x needs Phi_1=x-1. Because total degree is 4, only Phi_1,Phi_2,Phi_3,Phi_4,Phi_6 can occur. For each p>=5, p is coprime to each index and Phi_d(p)|Phi_d(p^p) by the exact identity Phi_d(x^p)=Phi_d(x)Phi_{pd}(x). Prime factorization at p=2 and p=3 gives precisely the four linear constraints e1+e3>=e2+e6, e2>=e4, e1>=e3 and e2>=e6. Direct independent enumeration of the 12 admissible exponent vectors (by cyclotomic degree: 1,2,3,4; counts 1,2,3,6) agreed with exact evaluations at p=2,3,5,7,11. Filling degree with x-powers plus x^4 yields exactly 13. The symbolically universal p>=5 proof, not prime sampling, establishes all-prime sufficiency.
